title: Introduction to loops and while statements
recap: A while loop repeats its statement while its condition stays true. The condition is checked before every iteration, so the body may run zero times.
A loop variable counts the iterations. Updating it inside the body is what eventually ends the loop, and forgetting that step creates an infinite loop.
objectives: Implement sumUpTo from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement sumUpTo with a while loop. Return the sum of every integer from 1 through limit, inclusive. Return 0 when limit <= 0. The tested limits are at most 1000, so the sum fits in int. You write the initialization, condition, accumulation, and increment yourself.
hints: Keep a total and a current integer starting at 1.
Continue while the current integer is <= limit.
Increment the current integer inside the loop to avoid an infinite loop.
